screen-recording.promise: Once capture reports a failure, later frame callbacks append no more frames.
screen-recording.harm: An unacknowledged stop can let a callback reach a finalized video writer.
screen-recording.scope: One stream, one accepted frame, one stream failure, and one late callback; acknowledgement and timeout are distinct. The replay runs actual callback, stop and finish methods with fake framework objects. It does not record a real display or prove ScreenCaptureKit callback timing.
screen-recording.mutation: Remove the callback failure guard; a failed stream must then append a frame.

camera-capture.promise: A successful camera command explicitly stops its capture session before returning.
camera-capture.harm: An error exits before the deferred explicit stop; resource reclamation is left to process teardown.
camera-capture.scope: One session, one frame, permission denial, frame timeout and encoding/write failure. The replay extracts the actual start/defer/first-frame block; conversion and disk-write failures share the same Out.fail abstraction but are not individually injected. OS cleanup on process exit is outside the explicit-cleanup invariant.
camera-capture.mutation: Remove the deferred session stop; a successful capture must lose its stop event.

file-operations.promise: Dry-run exits with a preview, and file moves require confirmation; every planned item is accounted for once.
file-operations.harm: A preview that enters the confirmation or mutation branch can mislead an agent or touch user files.
file-operations.scope: Two selected cache entries with independent success/failure. The replay executes the actual cleaner body with a fake filesystem and real output/confirmation logic. Target discovery, app-uninstall matching, Downloads collisions, permanent Trash emptying, settings import and concurrent filesystem replacement are excluded.
file-operations.mutation: Bypass the dry-run branch; preview must incorrectly request noninteractive confirmation.

dmg-install.promise: Replacing an existing application requires explicit approval.
dmg-install.harm: A copy failure can remove the previous app and bypass image ejection; failed input cleanup can still be reported as successful.
dmg-install.scope: One existing app and one image; mount, find-app, confirmation, removal, copy, cleanup and detach are separate steps. The actual command body runs against fake filesystem and process dependencies. No disk image is mounted; subprocess internals, crash recovery and concurrent installs are excluded. Detach failure is represented but no unconditional successful-detach guarantee is asserted.
dmg-install.mutation: Force confirmation to yes; an unapproved command must delete the fake destination.

fan-control.promise: A successful manual target write must have matching readback within two RPM.
fan-control.harm: The manual-control bit can remain set after a later target write or readback fails.
fan-control.scope: One valid fan, a validated in-range RPM, optional forced-bit support, and accepted/rejected/mismatching firmware responses. Actual Set.run executes against fake SMC dependencies. Physical cooling, SMC encoding, range arithmetic, concurrent commands, fans auto and audio routing are excluded.
fan-control.mutation: Remove the readback tolerance guard; ignored writes must incorrectly report success.

keep-awake.promise: Normal completion releases the acquired sleep-prevention assertion.
keep-awake.harm: Ctrl-C can remain queued on the main dispatch queue while the synchronous main thread sleeps indefinitely.
keep-awake.scope: One assertion; duration/PID completion and indefinite SIGINT waiting. The actual run body uses fake IOPM calls, real signal dispatch and Thread.sleep; the child is killed after SIGINT fails to complete. No real power assertion is acquired. PID reuse, EPERM, wall-clock jumps and SIGTERM are excluded.
keep-awake.mutation: Remove the deferred assertion release; normal timed completion must retain it.

usage-index.promise: A partial transcript line remains available for parsing after it is completed.
usage-index.harm: Incremental Codex scans add cumulative totals and overstate usage: 10 followed by 15 becomes 25.
usage-index.scope: One file, two usage records, unchanged reuse, a partial-line completion and full reindex. Values 1/2 in the model represent 10/15 in the real source replay. Arithmetic and parsing execute on actual source over scratch JSONL fixtures. Same-size rewrites, cross-process index writes, budget edges, malformed JSON and today-by-mtime semantics are excluded.
usage-index.mutation: Resume an append at the old file size instead of parsedBytes; the partial last line must be lost.

terminal-session.promise: After a normal quit or handled fatal signal from the active dashboard, terminal settings and cursor visibility are restored.
terminal-session.harm: A failed restore leaves the shell in raw input or hides its cursor.
terminal-session.scope: One terminal session: piped output, saved settings, raw mode, alternate screen, normal quit, handled fatal signal, idempotent cleanup. The complete TUI enum is compiled from source and tested on real pseudo-terminals with q and SIGTERM; all termios fields and the cursor/alternate-screen restore sequence are compared. SIGKILL, startup signals before failsafe registration, resize and Unicode input are excluded.
terminal-session.mutation: Lose the saved-termios flag; q and SIGTERM must fail restoration.
